intended_object: Take a finite extension L/K of number fields and a finite place v of K. The intended object is the group of semi-local integral units: the subgroup of (K_v ⊗_K L)^× that the decomposition K_v ⊗_K L ≅ ∏_{w|v} L_w identifies with ∏_{w|v} O_{L_w}^×. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation, which follow Milne, Class Field Theory VII §2.
explanation:
The definition is an infimum over the places w of L lying over v. For each w it takes the preimage of the depth-zero unit filtration U^0(L_w) = O_{L_w}^× under the map (K_v ⊗ L)^× → L_w^×. That map is the w-th component of the library's semi-local isomorphism `semilocalEquiv`, K_v ⊗_K L ≃ ∏_{w|v} L_w. A unit therefore lies in the subgroup exactly when each of its components has valuation 1, which is what the lemma `mem_semilocalIntegralUnits_iff` states. That is the standard group ∏_{w|v} O_{L_w}^× seen inside (K_v ⊗_K L)^×.

The number-field setting is the one `semilocalEquiv` is built in: its bijectivity proof uses the degree formula Σ_{w|v} [L_w : K_v] = [L : K]. It is also the setting of the library's idelic cohomology. The same construction could be written for more general Dedekind extensions, but number fields are its standard home here, and Mathlib has no general version.

Mathlib has no definition of this semi-local subgroup.
